title: Prove a stable 8n+4 tensor-width test for full dyadic Clifford programs
body:
Fixed native identities can agree at small tensor widths and fail later. This PR proves that, on `n` binary axes, equality at **every width from 1 through 8n+4** is equivalent to equality at **all positive widths** for complete scalar register programs over the full dyadic Clifford group. The cutoff is independent of program length and expanded support. It includes the source Gaussian and Hadamard gates.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/PROOF.md) gives more than a zero test: some tested width has normalized squared Hilbert-Schmidt residual at least **14/15 of the squared coefficient norm**, after equal exact operators are combined. A rational trace filter recovers that coefficient norm from the finite norm sequence. The [producer](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/certify.py) uses base-space Gram traces and extracts a concrete nonzero tensor entry without building a tensor matrix. Start with the [guide](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/README.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/RESULT.json) and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/SOURCES.json).

This is an **enabling proof and reusable exact verifier**. This PR does not change the [selected conditional kappa](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/certificates/selected-result.json), now **15108879/5000000000 = 0.0030217758** after the separate maintainer admission of [PR #4610](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4610) through [PR #5241](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5241). There is no supplier admission in this package. Physical layout, stock, precision, tapes and outer recovery remain separate obligations.

The class consists of unitary matrices over `Z[i,1/2]` that normalize the Pauli group, with exact global phase retained. All dirty inputs and returns are independent. Programs and scalar coefficients are fixed as width varies; coefficients stay outside tensor powers. The proof allows complex coefficients; the implementation uses exact Gaussian rationals. Width-dependent programs, non-Clifford gates, nonunitary operator scalings, restricted clean inputs, rectangular types and nonlinear or rounded leaves are outside the contract. Compilation can expand exponentially many terms, and the base dimension is `2^n`; no polynomial-time circuit solver or practical full-supplier speedup is claimed.

The complete 96-element one-axis group gives a useful counterexample: its Reynolds average vanishes at widths **1 through 7** and has rank **15 at width 8**, with a literal entry **5/24**. The [example certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/examples/reynolds.certificate.json) records the roles and coordinates. A [separate signed-word checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/check_witness.py) checks that literal entry without importing the producer or using its trace argument. It shares the frozen scalar arithmetic and does not certify the universal theorem or reported norms.

Validation used CPython 3.12.13 on macOS, with no third-party packages:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-tensor-gram
python3.12 -I -B research/clifford-tensor-gram/audit_mutations.py
python3.12 -I -B research/clifford-tensor-gram/check_witness.py research/clifford-tensor-gram/examples/reynolds.json research/clifford-tensor-gram/examples/reynolds.certificate.json
```

The registered runner passes normal and optimized modes, each printing `PASS_CLIFFORD_TENSOR_GRAM_NO_NEW_KAPPA`, then reports `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/clifford-tensor-gram outcome=completed`. The other commands print `PASS_CLIFFORD_GRAM_MUTATIONS` and `PASS_LITERAL_TENSOR_WITNESS 5/24`.

- Exact coverage: all 96 one-axis operators, 689 trace-filter values, 2,124 source columns including both nine-axis Gaussian orientations, 48 entangling trace cases, 60 explicit tensor norms, 72 complete endpoint comparisons, 24 full tensor program comparisons, 16 random literal witnesses, two zero-axis cases and 20 rejection controls.
- The [mutation receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d/research/clifford-tensor-gram/MUTATIONS.json) records four private-copy mathematical defects rejected in both modes: a missing trace factor, ignored inverse, omitted dirty return and missing Gram normalization.
- Committed-byte checks and official 22-file export integrity pass. Both exported modes also pass with Git absent from PATH and the export read-only; all 23 regular files, including its export manifest, remain unchanged. Export SHA-256: `a022640fa120addd1b0d852dc21bdafa9fb1276ecc3d41e34ece5665d90dc6c5`.

Finite checks corroborate the written uniform proof. No selected cold replay, complete provider, Lean, Docker, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. The optional full-history preflight was omitted in this shallow checkout; recorded source objects and bytes were checked, and the declared base is an ancestor of this contribution.

Base: canonical main at session start, `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority revision 7. Exact contribution head: `0db0609042d3bee25028ef6515fcee40a33e958d`. Both consumed source files remain pinned to that base. The submission refresh reached `1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4`: its new frontier review and priorities were read; priority revision 7 and both dependencies are unchanged. The base's selected record is historical provenance, not the current selection. No predecessor, shared control or selected record is modified by this PR. The final overlap snapshot covered 322 open PRs and 4,657 Discussion records with complete remote pagination; relevant source proofs were read separately. Arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits. The [canonical claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5236#discussioncomment-19153620) records the scope.

This package supplies the explicit cutoff and stability bound for fixed programs.
- Concurrent [PR #5369](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5369) proves a four-width criterion for the smaller affine-quadratic monomial class. Its proof, complexity result and event fixture remain separate; its scope excludes Hadamard gates. The [coordination pointer](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5354#discussioncomment-19153650) records this distinction.

Burnside-Brauer tensor generation, Pauli conjugation, Gaussian-integer factorization and Gram interpolation are classical; the proof cites their context. No global literature priority is claimed. New work by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. The guide leaves concrete next steps for phase-exact tableau traces, a sharp cutoff and a complete provider adapter.
